findings.title: "Ready xor failed" invariant comment is contradicted by the operation-error path
findings.description: `MountState`'s doc comment states "`ready` and `error` … are never independent — a chart is ready xor failed — … committed together in a single state update," and `src/chart/use-chart-provider.ts` repeats the claim ("a chart is ready xor failed … no window in which a stale `ready` is paired with a fresh `error`"). The code deliberately violates it: `setOperationError` (use-chart-provider.ts) commits `error` alone while keeping `ready: true`, `use-chart-provider.errors.test.tsx` asserts "A post-mount operation failure does not un-ready a live chart," and `chart-route.tsx` renders the chart *and* the error alert simultaneously by design. The behavior is correct and tested; only the invariant comment is wrong. Since this project leans on comments as load-bearing design documentation, a maintainer reading "ready xor failed" could "fix" the code to match the comment (e.g., un-ready the chart on an operation error), breaking the tested UX. Reword the comment to state the actual invariant: mount outcomes are committed atomically and are ready-xor-failed, while post-mount operation errors set `error` without disturbing `ready`.

findings.title: smoke spec header cites the wrong e2e spec for the "/" chart
findings.description: The updated header comment says "The chart itself is asserted in chart-render.spec.ts; this spec covers the shell around it." `chart-render.spec.ts` targets the internal `/__chart-harness` route (slice 102); the product "/" chart is asserted by the new `chart-live.spec.ts` introduced in this same diff. Fix the cross-reference so the next maintainer lands in the right spec.

findings.title: Mid-file import statements in the translation test
findings.description: After the twelve top-of-file imports, `LINE_SERIES` is declared at lines 15–21 and then two more `import` statements appear at lines 22–23 (`./support/chart-provider-spy.ts`, `./support/render-with-contexts.tsx`). ESM hoisting makes this work, and Vitest's mock hoisting is unaffected (the `vi.mock` call is already at the top), but it breaks the project's import-sorting convention and the pattern every sibling suite in this diff follows. Move the two imports up with the rest.

findings.title: Hook file exceeds the ~300-line project guide
findings.description: The file is 366 lines against the project's "~300 lines where practical" guide. The extraction of `chart-operations.ts` (types) and `chart-facade.ts` (forwarding) already did the real splitting, and the remainder is dominated by lifecycle-justification comments rather than code, so this is close to the practical floor — but the ESLint suppression comment in `eslint.config.js` frames the current size as the *acceptable* outcome, so it is worth watching that the next seam (initiative 120's indicator translation) lands in a sibling module rather than growing this file further.

findings.title: File-scoped `react-hooks/refs` suppression is broader than the false positive it documents
findings.description: The suppression is unusually well documented (root cause, probe, and the rejected alternative are all recorded), which is good practice. The tradeoff not addressed in the comment: scoping via config disables the rule for *all future code* in `src/chart/use-chart-provider.ts`, not just the memoized-closure false positives. Since the rule fires on specific lines (the `series`/`chart` `useMemo` calls), `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/refs` on those lines would keep the rule armed for everything else added to the file later. I could not execute ESLint to confirm the rule's exact report locations, so this is a suggestion rather than a verified defect.
